tagline: Across Johns Island, past a very old oak.
intro: Bohicket Road runs ten miles down Johns Island, the largest island in South Carolina, toward Kiawah and Seabrook. Building on those two islands has made it a busy road, but SCDOT still counts it handsome, with historical, recreational and farm sites along the way.

The island took its name from Saint John Parish in Barbados, where its first English settlers came from. Before them were the Kiawah, the Stono and the Bohicket, and the island is still known for its farms and its tomatoes.

moments.title: Angel Oak
moments.text: A southern live oak thought to be more than four centuries old throws shade over 17,200 square feet, its longest branch reaching 187 feet.

moments.title: Johns Island Presbyterian Church
moments.text: First built in 1719 and enlarged in 1792 and 1823, it is one of the oldest wood-frame churches in the country.
